text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that the next general elections in Hungary should be held in May 1998 and complained that no dialogue similar to what exists in Western democracies can be established with the opposition. @

- An offensive is shortly to be launched to sell Hungarian agricultural goods on foreign markets, Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy said at press conference in the Agricultural Marketing Centre, a new state organ aiming to foster exports by subsidising marketing activities.

- The directors of EBRD and GE Capital, major owners of Budapest Bank, expressed their surprise at the fact that the bank's privatisation contract, concluded a year ago, is still the object of debate. @
- The national telephone company Matav, which operates 70-80 percent of the country's phone lines, generated HUF 23 billion post-tax profits last year on revenues of HUF 194 billion.
- According to preliminary data, after tax profits of the iron industry group Dunaferr amounted to HUF 4.3-4.4 billion.
- A 25.8 percent stake in the sugar factory Petohazi Cukoripari Kft. is to be purchased by Betacukor Investment Kft.
- Influenza epidemic has so so far claimed 10 fatalities. @
- Two drivers were killed and 23 passengers were injured when a Romanian and an Italian motorcoach collided on Wednesday on Route 42.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The vice president of the Young Democrats said on Wednesday there aren't any serious chances for cooperation between four of the five parliamentary opposition parties ahead of the forthcoming general elections.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn is on a one-day visit to the Netherlands today. @
- An auction today will see the debut of a state bond maturing in five years, the longest period among fixed-interest state securities so far.
- The brokerage firm ING Baring Securities posted the top trading turnover, HUF 294 billion, on the stock exchange in the second half of 1996.
- The 1996 after tax profits of chemical company Pannonplast reached HUF 1.42 billion, exceeding the previous year's figure by 70 percent. @
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The Hungarian-EU Associate Committee will hold two days of talks today and Friday to discuss the progress of Hungary's preparation for accession to the EU.
- Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ferenc Vegh is slated to open talks in Brussels today on Hungarian armed forces reform and defence goals. @
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Addressing a joint function staged by the American and British Chambers of Commerce, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said the cabinet is working to resolve Hungary's dispute with the U.S. and other states who filed a complaint against Hungary with the WTO.
- The country's energy consumption increased by 2.1 percent last year to 1,090 petajoules, the Energy Information Agency reports. @
- A recent study by Deutsche Bank has found that Hungary's banking sector is more developed than that of the Czech Republic or Poland, but each three are still far below Western levels.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
